title: Cloud Summit Toronto 2026
description:
The first Toronto edition of Cloud Summit, a community-run multi-cloud conference from the Canadian Public Cloud Association.

The day takes over seven levels of the Northeastern University campus on Queen Street West, with keynote sessions, technical tracks, workshops and a sponsor floor. The HackerRivals hackathon runs alongside it as a three-hour competition.

One ticket also covers Toronto AWS Day, held at the same venue on the same day. Doors are at noon and the after party starts at 6:30 PM.
location: Northeastern University Toronto, 375 Queen St W, Toronto, ON M5V 2A5

title: Toronto Big Business, Tech and Entrepreneur Professional Networking Soiree
description:
An after-work mixer for tech startups, entrepreneurs, business owners and professionals, run by the Toronto Entrepreneurs, Startup & Business Coalition.

The format is open networking over three hours at a St. Clair Avenue lounge. People come to find co-founders, partners, coaches or team members rather than to hear talks.

Entry is free but you must RSVP in advance.
location: Gatherings Bar And Lounge, 49 St Clair Ave W, Toronto, ON M4V 1K7

title: Women in Tech Toronto 2026
description:
An evening for mid-level and senior women in tech, run by OutGeekWomen, where the job seekers set the agenda rather than the recruiters.

CTOs and hiring teams give short pitches about their companies, then the rest of the night is open networking. It is aimed at software engineers, AI and ML specialists, data scientists, product managers and cybersecurity professionals.

Runs 6:00 PM to 8:30 PM downtown.

title: Financial Affiliate Marketing Forum 2026
description:
A one-day forum for performance marketers working in Canadian financial services.

It brings together banking leaders, fintech operators and affiliate marketers for strategy sessions, practical talks and networking. Topics cover how regulated financial brands acquire customers through partner and affiliate channels.

The day runs 8:30 AM to 6:00 PM Eastern at The Quay on the waterfront.
location: The Quay, 100 Queens Quay E, 3rd Floor, Toronto, ON M5E 1Z2

title: SecTor 2026
description:
Canada's largest cybersecurity conference, now in its 20th year and part of the Black Hat family of events.

SecTor is built around research talks from practitioners: underground threats, attack techniques and the corporate defences that answer them. The programme mixes training days, briefings, an expo floor and community villages.

It runs October 6 to 8, 2026 at the Metro Toronto Convention Centre.
location: Metro Toronto Convention Centre, 255 Front St W, Toronto, ON M5V 2W6

title: Canadian Lenders Summit 2026
description:
An annual gathering of lending leaders from banking, credit unions, private lending and fintech.

Sessions cover risk management, AI in lending, regulatory compliance, consumer credit and business financing, with practical tracks on fraud prevention, mortgage modernisation, SMB credit and capital sourcing.

The day runs 8:00 AM to 6:00 PM, with a three-hour reception from 2:00 PM.
location: The Quay, 100 Queens Quay E, 3rd Floor, Toronto, ON M5E 1Z2

title: WomenHack Toronto
description:
A one-evening hiring event where women technologists meet 15 to 20 employers in rapid one-on-one rounds.

The format is speed-interviewing rather than a career fair: short scheduled conversations with each company, then open networking. It is aimed at engineers, designers and other technical roles.

Free for candidates. Places are by application, so apply for an invite before the date.

title: Difinity Conference Toronto 2026
description:
Difinity is a Microsoft Data, AI, Power BI and Fabric conference that has run in New Zealand since 2017. This is its first Canadian edition.

The programme runs over two days: a pre-conference day on September 10 and the main conference day on September 11. Speakers come from the Microsoft product team, plus MVPs, Regional Directors and industry practitioners.

It is aimed at anyone working in data analytics: developers, business analysts, BI professionals, database administrators, architects, IT decision makers and consultants.
location: Microsoft Toronto, Suite 4400, 81 Bay St, Toronto, ON M5J 0E7

title: TechTO: Together Toronto
description:
TechTO is one of Toronto's longest-running tech community events, built around in-depth conversations with local founders, operators and investors.

This edition runs a community open mic, short speaker talks and a fireside chat, followed by an off-site after party. Hosts include TechTO co-founders Alex Norman and Jason Goldlist, plus general manager Megha Kandoi.

Tickets are $30 early bird and free for TechTO members; food and drink are included.
location: Schwartz Reisman Innovation Campus, 108 College St, Toronto, ON M5G 0C6

title: Toronto Tech Mixer and Social
description:
A weekly after-work drinks and networking meetup for people working in tech, AI, data and IT, hosted by Toronto Tech Social.

It runs every Friday from 6:00 PM at Paupers Pub on Bloor Street West. The format is deliberately informal: no talks, just tables of software developers, data and ML people, IT staff, designers and product folks meeting each other.

Entry is $5 and must be booked online in advance; there are no tickets at the door.
location: Paupers Pub, 539 Bloor St W, Toronto, ON

title: AI Summit 2026 - Toronto AI Meetup
description:
A one-evening summit run by the Toronto AI Meetup, focused on agentic AI in production rather than model theory.

The programme includes hands-on workshops on running AI agents in production and on agentic memory, followed by expert panels on what is helping and hurting AI adoption inside companies. An invite-only roundtable for senior leaders runs before the main event.

Doors open at 5:15 PM with registration and networking over light snacks. Attendees must also RSVP and sign the consent form on the organiser's Luma page to get in.
location: OneEleven, 345 Front St W, 4th Floor, Toronto, ON

title: Elevate Festival 2026
description:
Elevate is Canada's largest tech and innovation festival, running September 22-24, 2026 in downtown Toronto.

The 2026 edition expects more than 10,000 attendees and over 250 speakers across seven content tracks, with startup and investor programming, curated lounges, roundtables and matchmaking for meetings.

Announced speakers include Christian Weedbrook (Xanadu), Mati Staniszewski (ElevenLabs), Vivek Sagi (Bumble), Lior Ron (Waabi) and Michael Pelosi (Cohere).

title: M365 Toronto 2026
description:
A community-run Microsoft cloud conference held at Microsoft's Canadian headquarters in downtown Toronto.

Sessions cover AI, the modern workplace, business applications and the wider Microsoft 365 stack, delivered by Microsoft MVPs and community speakers. The day includes keynotes, breakout sessions and time to meet other practitioners.

Doors open at 8:00 AM. The event is part of the Community Days network of Microsoft community conferences.
location: Microsoft Canada Headquarters, 4400-81 Bay St, Toronto, ON

title: MCP Dev Summit Toronto
description:
A Linux Foundation technical summit for engineers building real-world agentic AI systems, with the Model Context Protocol (MCP) as the common foundation.

Talks and case studies cover agent architecture and orchestration, multi-agent systems, MCP protocol development, enterprise integration, and the practical problems of running agents securely and reliably in production.

The event runs October 5-6, 2026. Each day mixes keynotes, breakout sessions and a solutions showcase, with an attendee reception on the first evening.

title: Generative AI Summit Toronto
description:
An engineering-focused summit for teams moving generative AI prototypes into production, run by the AI Accelerator Institute.

The day opens with a headliner stage from 9:00 AM to 10:30 AM, then splits into two tracks from 11:00 AM to 5:00 PM: a Generative AI track on turning model capabilities into scalable applications, and an Agentic AI track on building systems that can reason, act and finish real tasks. One ticket covers all stages.

Expect around 350 builders and engineers, plus hands-on workshops and roundtables on evaluation, reliability, tooling, governance and scale.
location: Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre, 525 Bay St, Toronto, ON

title: Product-Led Summit Toronto
description:
A two-day product leadership summit from Product-Led Alliance, running November 12-13, 2026.

Sessions look at what product leadership means now that AI has changed what building a product involves, budgets are tighter and product leaders are expected to own outcomes rather than roadmaps. Themes include shipping AI products that solve real customer problems, making a roadmap case a CFO will fund, and structuring teams to move quickly.

Each day has keynotes on the main stage plus a panel and interactive roundtables. Registration and breakfast open at 8:00 AM, with opening remarks at 9:00 AM.
location: Marriott Downtown at CF Toronto Eaton Centre, 525 Bay St, Toronto, ON

title: MongoDB.local Toronto
description:
A one-day MongoDB technical event for developers, architects, IT professionals and DevOps engineers building modern applications.

Content covers building and scaling applications in the AI era, reducing operational risk and speeding up delivery, with MongoDB engineers on hand throughout the day.

A full-day pass is $100 CAD and includes all sessions plus food and drink.
